title: one-mouth-answers-the-learning-question
what: Two charter fields answer 'how does this component learn?' — `learns` and `how_it_learns` — they disagree in 70 of 70 charters and flatly contradict each other (yes vs no) in 36, and the sieve that was built to enforce the question reads green over all of them because it checks presence, not agreement.
why: A charter is what a mind arriving cold reads to know what a component is (Law 5 — the address carries what a mind needs NOW). 36 of them currently tell that mind both 'this component does not learn' and 'yes, it learns, here is how', in the same file, and the check built to guarantee the question was answered reads green over every one. The lived symptom is a reader's, and it is the worst kind: not a missing answer, which you notice, but two answers, which you resolve by picking one — and whichever you pick, you were as likely to be wrong as right. Worse for a peer than a red would be, exactly as Law 8 says.
how: One field survives and the sieve reads it. THE EVIDENCE SAYS WHICH: `how_it_learns` is the considered answer, present in 70 of 73 charters and carrying reasoning ('By measured launch outcomes, not preference: a default (200K vs 1M) is a gate that moves only when a launch is...'); `learns` is the 2026-08-31 backfill and carries a generic dismissal in its place ('It does not; launchers are systemd unit files — static configuration'). So: (1) learning_declared at cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py:2884 reads `how_it_learns`, not `learns`; (2) the 3 charters carrying only `learns` are migrated to `how_it_learns`; (3) `learns` is removed from all 70, and a tooth refuses its return, because a retired field that can be re-added is a second mouth waiting to reopen; (4) the sieve gains the tooth its own docstring says it lacks — today it returns [] on an unparseable charter, which is a silent green over a corrupt file. WHAT THIS TICKET DOES NOT DO is judge content quality; the sieve's jurisdiction stays presence-and-single-mouth, and 'it doesn't, because X' stays a valid answer.
traces_to: Law 5 — 'The thing and the story of the thing may live in two roots; what they may never do is contradict each other.' Here they contradict each other INSIDE ONE FILE, 36 times. Also Law 8: learning_declared is a green a peer leans on, and a false green is worse here than a red because a red is distrusted by construction. And Law 1: the question 'does this component learn?' was answered once per charter and then answered again, differently, by a backfill.
falsifier: DONE when exactly one field answers the question across all 73 charters, when learning_declared reads that field, when a tooth refuses the retired field's return, when the sieve reds rather than passes on an unparseable charter, and when the count of self-contradicting charters measures 0 by the same script that measured 36 today. WRONG INTENT if the fix is to make the two fields agree rather than to remove one — that leaves two mouths that can drift apart again and buys one clean measurement at the price of the defect returning silently. Also WRONG if the surviving text is the backfill's: keeping `learns`'s generic dismissals over `how_it_learns`'s reasoning would satisfy every check in this falsifier while destroying the answers the question was asked for.
children: none, because the three pieces — repoint the sieve, migrate 70 charters by reading each pair, add two teeth — share one address (the inspector plus the charters it reads) and one measurement. Splitting them would let the charters migrate while the sieve still reads the retired field, which is the window in which the corpus reds wholesale for a bookkeeping reason.

out: MAKING THE TWO FIELDS AGREE instead of removing one. Hard bound: agreement-checking blesses the duplication and converts a structural defect into a maintenance obligation — two mouths kept in sync by a check are still two mouths. This is the fix a builder will propose because it is smaller.

A SCRIPTED FIELD RENAME. The migration reads each pair. A sed over 70 files satisfies every clause of the falsifier and takes the backfill's dismissals with it — the one outcome that would look like success and be the failure.

Judging CONTENT QUALITY. The sieve's jurisdiction stays presence-and-single-mouth; 'it doesn't, because X' remains a valid, complete answer. A sieve that rates the depth of a learning answer is a different ticket and probably a bad one.
Renaming the surviving field to something better. The name was inherited rather than chosen and that is recorded, not acted on — 70 uses is churn against a settled word.

Reopening 8820913d7a09-learning-as-a-pattern. It is PROVED and stays PROVED; its sieve survives, reading a different field and gaining a tooth. This ticket is what that build left behind, not a reversal of it.

decisions.text: D1: learning_declared (cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py, def learning_declared, registered in SIEVES under the same name) reads how_it_learns and only that: a non-blank string passes. Three ways to red, all under method learning_declared so the jurisdiction stays one sieve: (a) how_it_learns absent, None or blank -> claim "charter answers 'how does this component learn?'" expected True actual False; (b) the charter carries the retired key learns at all, whatever its value -> claim "charter answers the learning question with one mouth (learns is retired)" expected True actual False, finding field retired='learns'; (c) the charter cannot be read or parsed (OSError, JSONDecodeError, or a top-level value that is not a dict) -> claim 'charter parses' expected True actual False, finding field error=<the exception text>. Every finding carries charter=<path>. The sieve never raises and never returns [] on a file it could not read.

decisions.text: D2: MEASURED 2026-09-18 at the build (the cast's 73/70/3 grew): 81 charters, 74 carry both fields, 6 carry only learns (cairn/devices/cairn, cairn/machines/corrosion, cairn/machines/counting_block, cairn/machines/exemptions, cairn/machines/installer, cairn/machines/openai_wire), 1 carries only how_it_learns (cairn/devices/codemother/0/tools/charter), 0 neither. Each of the 74 pairs was read (the pairs are dumped side by side before the migration): in every one how_it_learns is the reasoned answer and learns is the 2026-08-31 backfill's one-liner or an echo of it (bus_client's learns says 'see how_it_learns'; rehearsal's two texts are identical; artifact, cgroup and question carry authored prose in both and how_it_learns is the more specific), so how_it_learns survives VERBATIM in all 74 and learns is removed. In the 6 only-learns charters the learns text moves under how_it_learns verbatim and learns is removed. No text is rewritten, merged or shortened by this ticket.

Teeth (c) and (d) are separate tooth() names: 'learning_declared refuses the retired field' and 'learning_declared reds an unparseable charter'.

D5: the census is code, not a scratch script: cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/one_mouth_answers_the_learning_question.py exposes census(root: Path) -> dict with keys charters, both, only_learns, only_how_it_learns, neither, unparseable, contradictions, offenders (paths carrying learns, or neither, or unparseable). It walks every intention+why.json under root skipping any path containing /proofs/ or /scratch. contradictions counts charters where the two texts open in opposite shapes — the first 60 chars of one match the yes-shape r'^\s*(yes|the point|directly|through|by |reflexively|from |partly|barely)' and of the other the no-shape r'^\s*(it does not|it doesn.t|no\b|not yet|nothing|it holds nothing)' — the same first-clause yes/no reading the cast's 36 came from (it reads 36 over the 74 pairs today). python3 -m cairn.machines.build_inspector.probes.one_mouth_answers_the_learning_question prints the census as JSON; at PROVED it prints both=0 only_learns=0 neither=0 unparseable=0 contradictions=0 charters=81.

D6: the same module declares a frozen module-level PROBE (cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe) with why, trigger, to='harbor_master', body={'nexus': 'hypothesize', 'kind': 'efficacy'}, carry, enough, horizon=1000. It reads the live repo root (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]) unless context['roots']['cairn'] names another. trigger: census offenders non-empty. enough: offenders empty AND both == 0 AND the falsification run stands — the latest record of cairn/machines/build_inspector/validations/test_inspector.json is green and its evidence.teeth_green names 'learning_declared refuses the retired field'. carry: finding text, the census, offenders, ticket=owning_ticket('96f71a89a0fa'), against_falsifier and suggests strings. No thresholds= (HEAD's Probe has no such field; 336a781018ba declares them when it lands) and no numeric knob exists here. Proof teeth for it live in test_inspector.py: PROBE frozen with callable carry and enough; over a scratch root with one offender enough is False and trigger True; over a clean scratch root with a fixture validation naming the tooth enough is True.

D7: out, verbatim from constraints: no agreement check between two fields, no scripted rename, no content judgement; 'it doesn't, because X' stays a valid answer. The charter of build_inspector itself gains nothing new beyond its own learns removal (its how_it_learns already says the sieve set grows per caught failure). The PROVEME crossing runs on component cairn/machines/build_inspector and the proof is sealed under netns then hollow-measured against the writes_to set: inspector.py, test_inspector.py, the probe module, the 80 charters and the 3 other fixture proofs.

D8: correcting D2/D5's '36': with D5's two regexes over the first 60 chars, the census reads contradictions=27 over the 74 pairs on 2026-09-18 (both=74 only_learns=6 only_how_it_learns=1 neither=0 unparseable=0 offenders=80). The cast's 36 was a hand reading on 2026-09-09; the module's number is the one that stands, and the only number enough depends on is 0. The regexes are not tuned to reproduce 36.

D9: the Probe API is cairn/tools/base/probe.py — Probe(why, trigger, to, body, carry, enough, horizon) is a frozen dataclass; trigger(now, context) -> bool; carry(context) -> dict; enough(context) -> bool; once(context, key, compute) memoizes one read per pulse; owning_ticket(id) -> the ticket record for the carry. against_falsifier and suggests are plain string keys in the carry dict, not helpers. The template is cairn/tools/base/probes/the_casting_door_has_callers.py (23089d52d805, PROVED 2026-09-18) — copy its shape verbatim, swap the survey.

D10: the validation file cairn/machines/build_inspector/validations/test_inspector.json is a JSON LIST of records; the probe reads the LAST element d[-1]: d[-1]['verdict'] == 'green' and d[-1]['evidence']['teeth_green'] is a list of the printed tooth labels verbatim (strings); the tooth is named when any label contains 'learning_declared refuses the retired field'. On OSError/ValueError/TypeError the read returns False. carry(context) returns EXACTLY this dict: {'finding': <str, one of: '<n> charter(s) answer the learning question with two mouths' | '<n> charter(s) still carry the retired field learns' | 'a charter answers the learning question with no mouth, or cannot be read' | 'the sieve has not yet redded a deliberately reintroduced learns' | 'every charter answers once and the sieve has refused a second mouth'>, 'census': <the census dict minus offenders>, 'offenders': <list of repo-relative charter paths>, 'falsification_stands': <bool>, 'ticket': owning_ticket('96f71a89a0fa'), 'against_falsifier': <the ticket's WRONG INTENT clause as a str>, 'suggests': <str>}. enough(context) -> bool = offenders empty AND both == 0 AND falsification_stands. trigger(now, context) -> bool = offenders non-empty. The survey is read once per pulse via once(context, 'census', fn).

decisions.text: D11: the module is 200 lines in this order: docstring; from __future__ import annotations; import json, re; from pathlib import Path; from cairn.tools.base.probe import Probe, once, owning_ticket; _REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]; constants _OWNING_TICKET, _RETIRED='learns', _FIELD='how_it_learns', _VALIDATION (relative path), _TOOTH, _HORIZON=1000, _YES/_NO compiled regexes, _HEAD=60; def _repo_root(context) -> Path (context['roots']['cairn'] if present else _REPO_ROOT); def _charters(root) -> sorted list of root.rglob('intention+why.json') skipping any path containing '/proofs/', 'scratch' or '/.git/'; def _shape(text) -> 'yes'|'no'|''; def census(root=None) -> dict; def _falsification_stands(root) -> bool; def _survey(context) -> dict via once; def _enough(context); def _trigger(now, context); def _carry(context); PROBE = Probe(why=<str>, trigger=_trigger, to='harbor_master', body={'nexus': 'hypothesize', 'kind': 'efficacy'}, carry=_carry, enough=_enough, horizon=_HORIZON); if __name__ == '__main__': print(json.dumps(census(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)). Probe is a frozen dataclass — no attribute is set after construction.

decisions.text: D12: DISCOVERY: the 80 charters to migrate are exactly the paths listed in the decompose berth's fifth piece writes_to (/home/akien/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/decompose-20260918T121248-85cf34a9b0a3.json), which equals the output of: grep -rl '"learns"' --include=intention+why.json . | grep -v /proofs/ | grep -v scratch | sort (run at repo root before the migration; 80 lines; the 81st charter, cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs is excluded because it is a proof fixture — the census of 81 counts every non-proof charter, 80 of which carry learns and 1 carries only how_it_learns). KEY ORDER: the serializer does NOT preserve it automatically; the builder reconstructs by hand: read the charter with json.loads (dict preserves insertion order), then build a new dict iterating the old items in order: skip the key 'learns' — except when how_it_learns is absent or blank, in which case emit ('how_it_learns', <the learns text>) AT THE POSITION learns held and skip the blank how_it_learns key wherever it sits; every other key copied verbatim. Serialize with json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) plus a trailing newline iff the original ended with one (all 80 originals are indent=2 utf-8 — the raw diff against each original is exactly one deleted line for the 74 kept charters). Write that text to a scratch file and fire cairn artifact write --verb charter --why '96f71a89a0fa: one mouth answers the learning question' --from <scratch> <charter path> — never write_text at the charter path.
